writeup.headline: Welltower rates Hold at 45, right on the Sell edge, as strong growth meets weak balance sheet and valuation scores.
writeup.thesis: Welltower scores 45, the lowest point of the Hold band, so one point lower would make it a Sell. Growth is the clear strength (score 87), with latest-quarter revenue growth of 51.4% year on year and TTM revenue growth of 49.4%, and the company raised full-year 2026 normalized FFO guidance to $6.47–$6.53 per diluted share after a strong Q3. Against that, the balance sheet scores 8, with net debt at 7.63 times FCF and cash covering 0.13 of debt. Valuation scores 10: in absolute terms the shares look high at 14.6x sales and 80.1x FCF, with the FCF yield 3.7 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield. Against its own history the stock is expensive, more expensive than at 53 of the last 61 month-ends on P/FCF. Quality is also weak (28), with an operating margin of -22.9%, stock-based compensation at 13.7% of revenue and the diluted share count up 10.1% year on year.
key_risks: High leverage: net debt is 7.63 times FCF and cash covers only 0.13 of debt.
Rich absolute valuation, with P/FCF of 80.1x and the FCF yield 3.7 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield.
Ongoing dilution, with the diluted share count up 10.1% year on year, and stock-based compensation at 13.7% of revenue.
Negative operating margin of -22.9% despite fast revenue growth.
Heavy acquisition pace and operator changes such as the Brookdale deal, which removes about $17.8M of 2027 rent.
what_would_change: A 1-point drop in the score would move the rating to Sell, for example from a weaker trend score (the price is already 2.7% below its 50-day average) or softer news.
Reaching Buy needs 20 more points, which would require large gains in the valuation or balance sheet scores, such as a lower P/FCF or less net debt relative to FCF.
A slowdown from today's revenue growth of about 50% would hurt the growth score, which is the main support for the rating.
Better margins and less dilution would lift the quality score from 28.
